chunks: Al-Hasan ibn al-Sayqal asked him about the chickens of Mecca and its birds, so he said:
“Whatever does not glide, then eat it; and whatever glides, then leave it to its way.”

key_terms.سَبِيلَهُ: its way; let it go free
key_terms.يَصُفَّ: to glide or spread the wings in flight

ai.seo_question: Which birds of Mecca may be eaten according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the birds of Mecca, distinguishing between those that may be eaten and those that should be left alone based on their manner of flight. It reflects jurisprudential guidance related to lawful taking and eating within the sacred precinct context.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2382 - Al-Hasan ibn al-Sayqal asked Imam (as) about the chickens and birds of Mecca.
Imam (as) said: "
What does not glide (in flight), you may eat it, and what glides, let it go."
